title: Spectral cutoffs converge to a global completed homogeneous graph-tier flow

completed_flow.tier: G_n={(u,v): Omega Q^n u in H and Q^n v in H} for each fixed integer n>=0, restricted to the compatible-real homogeneous manifold.
completed_flow.uniform_cutoffs: Every P_N-truncated solution obeys the same H_0 and F_n estimates with constants independent of N.
completed_flow.difference_equation: delta=u_N-u_M satisfies delta''+Omega^2 delta+lambda s_N delta=-lambda(s_N-s_M)u_M.
completed_flow.coefficient_difference: |s_N-s_M|<= (||u_N||+||u_M||)||delta||, so the base-energy bound makes the forcing locally Lipschitz uniformly on every finite interval.
completed_flow.cauchy_estimate: A graph-energy estimate and Gronwall bound the finite-time G_n difference by the initial G_n spectral tails; strong P_N convergence makes those tails vanish.
completed_flow.global_limit: The cutoff flows converge on every finite time interval to a unique continuous two-sided global flow S_n(t) on G_n.
completed_flow.nested_compatibility: K1403 support invariance and uniqueness make S_(n+1) the restriction of S_n; data in every finite graph tier retain every tier.
completed_flow.boundary: This is a completed global unbounded-charge flow only on the homogeneous current-free manifold, not on the spatially dependent Maxwell-matter phase space.
